questions.text: What is the main function of protein in the body?
questions.solution: Protein is needed for growth, repair and maintenance of body cells and tissues; it can also give energy
questions.hint: Think about what a growing teenager or an injured athlete needs to build

options: Growth and repair of body cells and tissues
Providing the main source of energy
feedback: The main source of energy is carbohydrate
That is the job of calcium (with vitamin D)
That is a function of vitamin C

questions.text: Name the mineral needed for strong bones and teeth that is found in milk and cheese.
questions.solution: Calcium builds strong bones and teeth; dairy foods are a good source
questions.hint: Its name begins with 'cal'

feedback.iron: Iron is needed for red blood cells

questions.text: Which vitamin is mainly made in the skin by the action of sunlight?
questions.solution: Vitamin D is made in the skin when it is exposed to sunlight; it helps the body absorb calcium
questions.hint: This vitamin is sometimes called the 'sunshine vitamin'

feedback: Vitamin C comes from fruit and vegetables, not from sunlight

questions.text: Which mineral is needed to make haemoglobin in red blood cells?
questions.solution: Iron is needed to make haemoglobin, which carries oxygen in red blood cells
questions.hint: A lack of this mineral can cause anaemia

feedback: Calcium is for bones and teeth
Sodium controls water balance in the body

questions.text: Which nutrient, found in wholegrain foods, fruit and vegetables, keeps the digestive system healthy and prevents constipation? Give the nutrient.
questions.solution: Fibre (NSP) adds bulk and keeps food moving through the digestive system
questions.hint: Wholemeal bread has more of it than white bread

questions.text: How many main food groups are shown on the Eatwell Guide?
questions.solution: The Eatwell Guide has five main food groups, with fluids and foods to eat less often shown outside them
questions.hint: Picture the Eatwell plate and count its coloured sections; drinks and foods to eat less often sit outside it

questions.text: Which nutrient provides the most energy per gram?
questions.solution: Fat provides about 9 kcal per gram, more than twice as much as carbohydrate or protein
questions.hint: Compare the energy in a gram of oil with a gram of sugar

feedback: Carbohydrate is the main energy source, but fat gives more energy per gram

questions.text: Which pair contains only fat-soluble vitamins?
questions.solution: The fat-soluble vitamins are A, D, E and K; the B vitamins and vitamin C are water-soluble
questions.hint: Vitamin C and the B group dissolve in water

feedback: Vitamin D is fat-soluble, but vitamin C is water-soluble

questions.text: Which deficiency disease, which causes bleeding gums, is caused by a lack of vitamin C? Give the disease.
questions.solution: A lack of vitamin C causes scurvy, with bleeding gums and slow wound healing
questions.hint: Sailors on long voyages used to get it until they took citrus fruit with them

feedback.rickets: Rickets is caused by a lack of vitamin D or calcium
feedback.anaemia: Anaemia is caused by a lack of iron

questions.text: Which statement about high biological value (HBV) and low biological value (LBV) protein is accurate?
questions.solution: HBV proteins (such as meat, fish, eggs, soya and quinoa) contain all the essential amino acids; LBV proteins lack at least one
questions.hint: Think about which type has the complete set of essential amino acids

options: LBV protein contains all the essential amino acids; HBV protein lacks one or more
HBV protein comes only from plants; LBV only from animals
HBV protein contains all the essential amino acids; LBV protein lacks one or more
HBV protein contains more fat than LBV protein
feedback: That is the wrong way round
Most HBV proteins come from animals, though soya and quinoa are HBV

questions.text: Which food group on the Eatwell Guide should make up just over a third of what we eat, along with fruit and vegetables?
questions.solution: Starchy carbohydrates make up just over a third of the Eatwell Guide; fruit and vegetables make up just over another third
questions.hint: This group provides most of our energy

options: Beans, pulses, fish, eggs, meat and other proteins
Potatoes, bread, rice, pasta and other starchy carbohydrates
feedback: Oil and spreads are the smallest section of the Eatwell Guide

questions.text: Which water-soluble vitamin, found in citrus fruits, helps the body absorb iron? Give the vitamin, for example 'vitamin K'.
questions.solution: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) helps the body absorb iron, especially from plant foods
questions.hint: Oranges and kiwi fruit are rich in it

questions.text: Which type of fat is found mainly in plant oils and oily fish and is usually liquid at room temperature?
questions.solution: Unsaturated fats come mainly from plants and oily fish and are usually liquid (oils) at room temperature
questions.hint: Olive oil is a good example

feedback: Saturated fats come mainly from animals and are usually solid at room temperature

questions.text: Which mineral, added to toothpaste and some water supplies, helps to strengthen tooth enamel? Give the mineral.
questions.solution: Fluoride strengthens tooth enamel and helps prevent tooth decay
questions.hint: Check the ingredients list on a tube of toothpaste

questions.text: A vegan wants to get all the essential amino acids from two LBV proteins eaten together. Which meal does this?
questions.solution: Beans and wheat are LBV proteins that complement each other, giving all the essential amino acids (protein complementation)
questions.hint: Look for a meal combining a pulse and a cereal

feedback: Butter is an animal product, so it is not vegan, and it is mostly fat

questions.text: A teenage girl often feels tired and looks pale. A lack of which mineral is a common cause of this?
questions.solution: Tiredness and pale skin are signs of iron deficiency anaemia; teenage girls need more iron because of menstruation
questions.hint: Think about the mineral needed for red blood cells

questions.text: Which group of people is advised to take folic acid?
questions.solution: Folic acid (a B vitamin) reduces the risk of neural tube defects such as spina bifida in the developing baby
questions.hint: Folic acid helps the baby's spine and nervous system develop

options: Women who are trying to get pregnant or are in early pregnancy

questions.text: Which vitamin is lost most easily when vegetables are boiled for a long time?
questions.solution: Vitamin C is water-soluble and damaged by heat, so it leaches into cooking water
questions.hint: Which vitamin dissolves in water and is easily destroyed by heat?

feedback: Vitamin D is fat-soluble, so it is not lost into cooking water

questions.text: Older people are advised to take a supplement of which vitamin to keep bones healthy, especially in autumn and winter? Give the vitamin, for example 'vitamin K'.
questions.solution: Vitamin D helps absorb calcium; older people may make less of it from sunlight
questions.hint: The body makes it when skin is in sunlight, and there is less sunlight in winter

questions.text: A person eats very few dairy foods. Which nutrient might they be short of?
questions.solution: Milk, cheese and yoghurt are major sources of calcium
questions.hint: Which mineral are milk and cheese famous for?

questions.text: Which deficiency disease causes soft, weak bones and bowed legs in children because of a lack of vitamin D or calcium? Give the disease.
questions.solution: Rickets is caused by a lack of vitamin D or calcium in children
questions.hint: In adults the same problem is called osteomalacia

feedback.scurvy: Scurvy is caused by a lack of vitamin C

questions.text: Food A has 10 g of fibre per 100 g and food B has 2 g per 100 g. Adults are advised to eat 30 g of fibre a day. Which statement is accurate?
questions.solution: 200 g of food A gives 2 × 10 = 20 g, and 20 g is two thirds of 30 g
questions.hint: Work out the fibre in 200 g of food A, then compare it with 30 g

options: 100 g of food B gives a third of the daily fibre advice
100 g of food A gives all of the daily fibre advice
200 g of food A would provide two thirds of the daily fibre advice
Food B has more fibre than food A
feedback: 100 g of food B gives 2 g, which is only a fifteenth of 30 g

questions.text: A meal is a burger, chips and a cola. Which change would bring it closer to the Eatwell Guide?
questions.solution: Adding vegetables and replacing a sugary drink with water moves the meal towards the Eatwell Guide
questions.hint: Which food group is missing, and which item is high in sugar?

options: Adding extra salt to the chips
Swapping the cola for a milkshake with cream
Adding a side salad and swapping the cola for water

questions.text: Which vitamin is most likely to be lacking in a vegan diet that has no fortified foods or supplements?
questions.solution: Vitamin B12 is found naturally almost only in animal foods, so vegans need fortified foods or supplements
questions.hint: This vitamin is found naturally almost only in animal products

feedback: Vitamin C is plentiful in fruit and vegetables

questions.text: Which type of fatty acid, found in oily fish such as salmon and mackerel, helps keep the heart healthy? Give the name (omega-…).
questions.solution: Omega-3 fatty acids in oily fish help keep the heart healthy
questions.hint: Its number is lower than omega-6

questions.text: Which statement about saturated fat is accurate?
questions.solution: A diet high in saturated fat can raise blood cholesterol, increasing the risk of coronary heart disease
questions.hint: Think about what builds up in the arteries

options: Saturated fat is mainly found in plant oils and is liquid at room temperature
Eating too much can raise blood cholesterol and increase the risk of heart disease
Saturated fat is needed to absorb vitamin C
feedback: That describes unsaturated fat

questions.text: A teenager is growing quickly. Which pair of nutrients is especially important for building bone at this age?
questions.solution: Calcium builds bone, and vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium; teenagers build most of their peak bone mass
questions.hint: One is a mineral in milk, and the other helps the body absorb it

questions.text: Which macronutrient is the body's main source of energy and is stored in the liver and muscles as glycogen? Give the macronutrient.
questions.solution: Carbohydrate is the main energy source; spare glucose is stored as glycogen in the liver and muscles
questions.hint: Starchy foods such as pasta and bread are rich in it

feedback.protein: Protein is mainly for growth and repair

questions.text: Why is protein especially important for children?
questions.solution: Children are growing quickly, so they need protein for growth as well as repair and maintenance
questions.hint: Think about the main function of protein

options: Protein is their only source of energy
Protein means they need no carbohydrate
They are growing, so they need protein to build new cells and tissues

questions.text: Why is vitamin C important when eating iron-rich plant foods such as spinach?
questions.solution: Iron from plants (non-haem iron) is harder to absorb; vitamin C helps the body absorb it
questions.hint: Think about absorption: plant iron is harder for the body to take in

options: Vitamin C helps the body absorb non-haem iron from plant foods
Vitamin C replaces iron in red blood cells
Vitamin C stops iron being absorbed
Vitamin C turns iron into calcium
feedback: Vitamin C helps iron absorption; tannins in tea can reduce it

questions.text: Which statement about eating too much salt (sodium) is accurate?
questions.solution: A high salt intake is linked to high blood pressure, which increases the risk of stroke and heart disease
questions.hint: Think about the effect of salt on the circulatory system

options: Too much salt can raise blood pressure, increasing the risk of stroke and heart disease
Too much salt prevents dehydration in all cases
Too much salt is needed to absorb vitamin D

questions.text: Which statement about the Eatwell Guide is accurate?
questions.solution: The Eatwell Guide shows balance over a day or a week, not every meal; it does not apply to children under 2
questions.hint: Does every meal have to look like the plate?

options: Every single meal must match the guide exactly
The guide is designed for babies under 2
The guide shows the proportions of food groups for a balanced diet over a day or a week
The guide recommends cutting out a whole food group
feedback: The Eatwell Guide does not apply to children under 2

questions.text: Which statement about energy balance is accurate?
questions.solution: Energy balance means energy in (from food and drink) matches energy out (body functions and activity)
questions.hint: Think of energy in compared with energy out

options: Energy is only used when the body is asleep
Active people need less energy than inactive people
The body uses no energy at rest
Energy from food and drink should match the energy the body uses over time
feedback: Physical activity uses extra energy
The body uses energy all the time for breathing, heartbeat and warmth

questions.text: Which vitamin from the B group should women take before and during early pregnancy to reduce the risk of spina bifida? Give its name.
questions.solution: Folic acid (folate, vitamin B9) reduces the risk of neural tube defects such as spina bifida
questions.hint: Its name comes from the Latin for 'leaf', as leafy greens contain it

questions.text: What happens during gelatinisation?
questions.solution: In gelatinisation, starch granules absorb liquid, swell and break open when heated, which thickens sauces
questions.hint: This is what happens when cornflour thickens a sauce

options: Starch granules absorb liquid, swell and burst when heated, thickening the mixture
Proteins set when they are heated
Air is trapped in a mixture
feedback: That is caramelisation
That is coagulation

questions.text: What is the browning of sugar when it is heated called? Give the term.
questions.solution: Heating sugar until it melts and turns brown is caramelisation
questions.hint: Think of the sweet brown sauce made by heating sugar

feedback.dextrinisation: Dextrinisation is the browning of starch by dry heat

questions.text: Which method of heat transfer happens when heat passes through a solid, such as a metal pan?
questions.solution: Conduction is heat passing through a solid from particle to particle, such as through a pan base
questions.hint: The pan handle can get hot this way

feedback: Convection happens in liquids and gases
Radiation travels as infrared waves, as in grilling

questions.text: Which of these is a chemical raising agent?
questions.solution: Bicarbonate of soda (and baking powder) are chemical raising agents that release carbon dioxide
questions.hint: Look for the powder that reacts to release gas

feedback: Yeast is a biological raising agent
Steam is a mechanical (physical) raising agent

questions.text: Which protein network forms when wheat flour is mixed with water and kneaded? Give the term.
questions.solution: Gluten forms from the proteins glutenin and gliadin when flour is mixed with water and kneaded
questions.hint: People with coeliac disease must avoid it

questions.text: Which gas makes bread dough rise when yeast ferments?
questions.solution: Yeast ferments sugars and produces carbon dioxide gas, which makes the dough rise
questions.hint: It is the same gas we breathe out

questions.text: Which cooking method uses radiation from above to cook food?
questions.solution: Grilling cooks food by radiation (infrared heat) from above
questions.hint: Think of toasting under a hot element

feedback: Boiling uses convection in water

questions.text: Which statement about denaturation and coagulation is accurate?
questions.solution: Proteins first denature (unfold) and then coagulate (join and set), as when an egg cooks
questions.hint: Think about the order of what happens to egg white as it cooks

options: Coagulation is when a protein's structure unfolds; denaturation is when proteins join together and set
Denaturation is when a protein's structure unfolds; coagulation is when denatured proteins join together and set
Both mean starch thickening a sauce
feedback: Starch thickening is gelatinisation

questions.text: Which substance in egg yolk acts as the emulsifier in mayonnaise? Give its name.
questions.solution: Lecithin in egg yolk is an emulsifier that holds oil and vinegar together in mayonnaise
questions.hint: Its name starts with 'leci'

questions.text: Which raising agent mainly makes choux pastry and Yorkshire puddings rise?
questions.solution: The high water content turns to steam in a hot oven, making choux pastry and Yorkshire puddings rise
questions.hint: These mixtures contain a lot of liquid and are cooked in a very hot oven

questions.text: Which method of heat transfer heats water in a pan by currents of hot liquid rising and cooler liquid sinking?
questions.solution: Convection currents move heat through liquids and gases
questions.hint: This method needs a liquid or gas that can move

questions.text: When bread is toasted, dry heat breaks down starch into dextrins and the surface turns brown. Give the term for this.
questions.solution: Starch breaking down into dextrins under dry heat is dextrinisation
questions.hint: The term comes from 'dextrins'

feedback.caramelisation: Caramelisation is the browning of sugar, not starch

questions.text: Which flour is most suitable for making bread?
questions.solution: Strong flour has more protein, forming more gluten to trap carbon dioxide and give a good rise
questions.hint: Bread needs a stretchy protein network that can trap gas

options: Strong flour, which has a high protein content for gluten
Soft flour, which has a low protein content
Cornflour, which is almost pure starch
Self-raising flour, which has baking powder added
feedback: Soft flour suits cakes and pastry

questions.text: Which water-based cooking method keeps the most water-soluble vitamins in vegetables?
questions.solution: Steaming keeps food out of the water, so fewer water-soluble vitamins leach out
questions.hint: In which method is the food not sitting in the water?

questions.text: A white sauce is made by heating flour, butter and milk while stirring until it thickens. Which process thickens it?
questions.solution: Starch in the flour gelatinises as it is heated in the milk, thickening the sauce
questions.hint: Flour contains starch

questions.text: Egg white turns from clear and runny to white and firm when fried. Which process is this?
questions.solution: Heat denatures the egg proteins, which then coagulate (set)
questions.hint: Egg white is mostly protein

feedback: Gelatinisation involves starch, not protein

questions.text: When making shortcrust pastry, fat is rubbed into flour. What does this do?
questions.solution: Fat coats the flour, waterproofing it so less gluten forms: this is called shortening
questions.hint: Think about why shortcrust pastry crumbles instead of stretching like bread dough

options: Coats the flour particles, limiting gluten development so the pastry is short and crumbly
Develops long gluten strands for a chewy texture
Adds steam to make the pastry rise

questions.text: A cut apple turns brown when left in the air. Give the term for this process.
questions.solution: Enzymes in the cut fruit react with oxygen in the air, causing enzymic browning
questions.hint: Enzymes in the fruit react with oxygen in the air

questions.text: Which would slow down the browning of a cut apple?
questions.solution: The acid in lemon juice slows the enzymes that cause browning
questions.hint: Acid slows down the enzymes

options: Leaving it uncovered in a warm room

questions.text: Whisking egg whites traps tiny bubbles and stretches the proteins. Which raising agent is being added? Give the raising agent.
questions.solution: Whisking traps air, a mechanical raising agent
questions.hint: The bubbles come from the room around the bowl

questions.text: A cake is made by beating fat and sugar together until light and fluffy. What is this method called?
questions.solution: Beating fat and sugar together traps air: this is the creaming method
questions.hint: The mixture becomes pale and creamy

feedback: Rubbing in is used for pastry and scones

questions.text: A white sauce has lumps in it. What is the most likely cause?
questions.solution: Starch must be kept moving while it heats; otherwise granules stick together into lumps
questions.hint: Think about what stirring does while the sauce heats up

options: The sauce was stirred all the time
The sauce was not stirred enough, so starch granules clumped before they gelatinised

questions.text: Scrambled eggs are overcooked and watery liquid seeps out of them. What is this called?
questions.solution: Overheated proteins tighten and squeeze out liquid: this is syneresis
questions.hint: The proteins shrink and squeeze water out

questions.text: Baking powder is bicarbonate of soda mixed with an acid such as cream of tartar. Why is the acid added?
questions.solution: Acid plus bicarbonate releases carbon dioxide, and no soapy-tasting washing soda is left behind
questions.hint: Think about what is left behind when bicarbonate of soda is heated with no acid

options: The acid makes the mixture sweeter
The acid reacts with the bicarbonate to release carbon dioxide without leaving a soapy taste
The acid turns the cake brown

questions.text: A bread dough is left in a cold fridge and hardly rises. Why?
questions.solution: Cold slows yeast down but does not kill it; at warm temperatures it ferments faster
questions.hint: What conditions does yeast need to work well?

options: Cold kills all the yeast immediately
Yeast works very slowly at low temperatures, so little carbon dioxide is produced
Cold makes the dough produce steam
feedback: Cold slows yeast down but does not kill it; high heat kills yeast

questions.text: Oil and vinegar do not normally mix, but an emulsifier can hold them together. Give the term for the mixture formed.
questions.solution: An emulsion is a mixture of two liquids that do not normally mix, held together by an emulsifier
questions.hint: Mayonnaise is an example of this type of mixture

feedback.emulsifier: The emulsifier is the substance that holds them together; the mixture is an emulsion

questions.text: Which cooking method uses mainly convection, with hot air circulating around the food?
questions.solution: In an oven, hot air circulates around the food by convection (with conduction through the tray)
questions.hint: Think about where hot air moves around food

feedback: Grilling uses radiation
Shallow frying uses conduction through hot oil and pan

questions.text: Which gelling agent made from seaweed can be used instead of gelatine in vegetarian desserts? Give the name.
questions.solution: Agar (agar-agar) comes from seaweed and sets liquids like gelatine
questions.hint: It comes from the sea, not from animals

questions.text: Why does kneading bread dough improve the texture of the bread?
questions.solution: Kneading develops a strong, stretchy gluten network that traps carbon dioxide from the yeast
questions.hint: Think about the protein network in the dough

options: Kneading stretches and strengthens the gluten so it can trap carbon dioxide and rise
Kneading kills the yeast so the bread stays flat
Kneading gelatinises the starch before baking

questions.text: Why do vegetables lose some vitamin C when they are boiled?
questions.solution: Vitamin C dissolves in the cooking water and is damaged by heat; steaming or using less water reduces the loss
questions.hint: Is vitamin C water-soluble or fat-soluble?

options: Vitamin C is fat-soluble and melts out
Vitamin C is water-soluble and damaged by heat, so it leaches into the water
Boiling turns vitamin C into fibre
Vitamin C is destroyed only by freezing

questions.text: Which statement about cooking meat is accurate?
questions.solution: Meat proteins denature and coagulate when heated, so meat becomes firmer and loses some juice
questions.hint: Meat is mainly protein

options: Heat gelatinises the protein in meat into starch
Meat proteins are not affected by heat
Heat denatures and coagulates the proteins, so the meat firms up and shrinks
Heat turns the fat in meat into fibre

questions.text: Why is cornflour good at thickening a sauce?
questions.solution: Cornflour is nearly all starch, so it gelatinises easily and thickens without forming gluten
questions.hint: Which carbohydrate thickens liquids when heated?

options: Cornflour is high in gluten, which forms a stretchy network
Cornflour contains yeast, which produces gas
Cornflour is a fat that forms an emulsion
Cornflour is almost pure starch, which gelatinises when heated with liquid
feedback: Cornflour contains no gluten

questions.text: In a microwave oven, the microwaves make molecules of one substance in the food vibrate and heat up. Give the substance.
questions.solution: Microwaves make water molecules in food vibrate, producing heat
questions.hint: Food with more of this substance heats up quickly in a microwave

questions.text: A cake recipe uses far more bicarbonate of soda than needed. What is the most likely result?
questions.solution: Too much bicarbonate of soda leaves a soapy, bitter aftertaste and can give a yellow colour and coarse texture
questions.hint: Bicarbonate on its own leaves a residue with a strong taste

options: A soapy, bitter taste and a yellowish, open texture
A dense cake that does not rise at all
A pale cake with no change in taste

questions.text: Why is a small amount of salt added to bread dough?
questions.solution: Salt adds flavour, strengthens gluten and slows the yeast so the dough rises evenly
questions.hint: Salt does more than one job in a dough: think about the living raising agent and the protein network

options: Salt controls the yeast and strengthens the gluten, as well as adding flavour

questions.text: What is the temperature range of the 'danger zone', where bacteria multiply most quickly?
questions.solution: The danger zone is 5–63 °C; bacteria multiply fastest at about 37 °C
questions.hint: The lower number is the top of the fridge range and the upper number is the hot-holding temperature

feedback: 0–5 °C is the correct fridge temperature, where bacteria multiply slowly

questions.text: At what temperature should a fridge be kept?
questions.solution: A fridge should be 0–5 °C to slow the growth of bacteria
questions.hint: It must be below the start of the danger zone

feedback: −18 °C or below is the freezer temperature

questions.text: Name the food poisoning bacterium most associated with raw or undercooked eggs.
questions.solution: Salmonella is linked with raw or undercooked eggs and poultry
questions.hint: Its name begins with 'sal'

questions.text: At what temperature should a freezer be kept?
questions.solution: Freezers should be −18 °C or below; bacteria become dormant but are not killed
questions.hint: It is well below the freezing point of water

questions.text: In UK kitchens, which colour of chopping board is used for raw meat? Give the colour.
questions.solution: Red boards are for raw meat; blue for raw fish, yellow for cooked meat and green for salad and fruit
questions.hint: Think of the colour of raw meat

feedback.green: Green is for salad and fruit

questions.text: Food handlers must cover cuts with a plaster of a special colour so it is easy to spot if it falls into food. Give the colour.
questions.solution: Food handlers use blue plasters because very few foods are blue
questions.hint: Very few foods are this colour

questions.text: Which date mark is about food safety and is used on high-risk foods such as fresh chicken? Give the date mark.
questions.solution: Use by dates are about safety; food should not be eaten after this date
questions.hint: One date mark is about quality; the other is about safety

feedback.best before: Best before is about quality, not safety

questions.text: Which statement about 'use by' and 'best before' dates is accurate?
questions.solution: Never eat food after its use by date; food may still be safe after its best before date, but quality may drop
questions.hint: Which one appears on fresh chicken and milk?

options: Best before is about safety; use by is about quality
Use by is for tins; best before is for fresh meat
Use by is about safety; best before is about quality
feedback: That is the wrong way round

questions.text: In UK kitchens, which colour of chopping board is used for raw fish?
questions.solution: Blue boards are for raw fish
questions.hint: Think of the colour of the sea

feedback: Red is for raw meat
Brown is for vegetables
White is for bread and dairy

questions.text: In GCSE Food Preparation and Nutrition, food should be cooked until its core temperature reaches at least what temperature? Give the answer in °C.
questions.solution: Cooking until the centre reaches at least 75 °C kills most food poisoning bacteria
questions.hint: It is higher than the hot-holding temperature of 63 °C

mistakes.feedback: 63 °C is the hot-holding temperature, not the cooking target

questions.text: Which list contains only high-risk foods?
questions.solution: High-risk foods are moist, high in protein and ready to eat, such as cooked meat, cooked rice and dairy desserts
questions.hint: High-risk foods are usually moist, high in protein and eaten without further cooking

options: Cooked chicken, cooked rice and dairy desserts
Crisps, bread and unopened tinned beans

questions.text: Give the term for the transfer of bacteria from one food, surface or person to another food.
questions.solution: Cross-contamination is when bacteria are moved onto food from raw food, equipment, surfaces or hands
questions.hint: Think about raw meat juices dripping onto a salad

questions.text: Name the bacterium that can grow at fridge temperatures and is linked with soft cheeses and pâté.
questions.solution: Listeria can grow even at fridge temperatures and is linked with soft cheese and pâté
questions.hint: Pregnant women are advised to avoid certain foods because of it

feedback.salmonella: Salmonella is linked with eggs and poultry; it does not grow well in a fridge

questions.text: Where in a fridge should raw meat be stored?
questions.solution: Raw meat goes at the bottom, covered, so its juices cannot drip onto ready-to-eat food
questions.hint: Think about which way juices drip

options: Next to cooked meat on the middle shelf
feedback: Juices could drip onto food below

questions.text: In ideal conditions, one bacterium divides into two every 20 minutes. Starting with one bacterium, how many will there be after 1 hour? Give a number.
questions.solution: 1 hour = 3 lots of 20 minutes: 1 → 2 → 4 → 8
questions.hint: Double the number once for every 20 minutes

mistakes.feedback: The number doubles each time; it does not go up by 2
There are 3 divisions, but the number doubles each time

questions.text: One bacterium divides into two every 20 minutes. Starting with one, how many bacteria will there be after 2 hours? Give a number.
questions.solution: 2 hours = 6 lots of 20 minutes, so 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 64
questions.hint: Work out how many 20-minute periods are in 2 hours, then keep doubling

mistakes.feedback: The number doubles each time; it does not go up by 2
There are 6 divisions, but the number doubles each time

questions.text: A chef cuts raw chicken and then slices cucumber with the same knife without washing it. What is the main risk?
questions.solution: This is cross-contamination: bacteria from raw meat get onto food that will not be cooked
questions.hint: The cucumber will not be cooked before it is eaten

options: Bacteria from the raw chicken are transferred to the ready-to-eat cucumber

questions.text: Cooked rice is left at room temperature overnight. Which bacterium is the main risk?
questions.solution: Bacillus cereus spores survive cooking and multiply in cooked rice left warm, producing toxins
questions.hint: This bacterium is famous for reheated rice

questions.text: A food handler has a small cut on their hand. What should they do?
questions.solution: Cuts must be covered with a blue waterproof plaster to stop bacteria spreading and so it can be seen if it falls off
questions.hint: The plaster must be easy to spot in food

options: Leave it uncovered so it heals
Cover it with a blue waterproof plaster
Cover it with a skin-coloured plaster
Wash it in the food sink

questions.text: Hot food on a buffet must be held above which temperature to keep it out of the danger zone? Give the answer in °C.
questions.solution: Hot food must be kept above 63 °C, the top of the danger zone
questions.hint: It is the upper limit of the danger zone

mistakes.feedback: 5 °C is the lower limit of the danger zone, for cold food

questions.text: Where is the safest place to defrost a frozen chicken? Give the kitchen appliance.
questions.solution: Defrost raw chicken in the fridge, in a dish on the bottom shelf, so it stays out of the danger zone
questions.hint: Keep the chicken out of the danger zone while it thaws

questions.text: A fridge thermometer reads 9 °C. What does this mean?
questions.solution: 9 °C is above the 0–5 °C fridge range and inside the danger zone
questions.hint: Compare 9 °C with the correct fridge range

options: The fridge is at the correct temperature
The fridge is too cold and will freeze the food
The fridge is too warm, so bacteria can multiply faster
Bacteria are killed at this temperature

questions.text: A food probe shows that the centre of a chicken pie is at 68 °C. What should the cook do?
questions.solution: The core should reach at least 75 °C to be safe, so it needs more cooking
questions.hint: What core temperature should cooked food reach?

options: Serve it, as it is above 63 °C
Put it in the fridge straight away
Serve it, as bacteria are killed above 37 °C
Keep cooking until the centre reaches at least 75 °C
feedback: 63 °C is the hot-holding temperature, not the cooking target

questions.text: Which practice helps prevent cross-contamination in a kitchen?
questions.solution: Colour-coded equipment keeps raw and ready-to-eat foods apart
questions.hint: Think about how bacteria could travel from raw meat to food that will not be cooked

options: Using separate colour-coded boards and knives for raw and ready-to-eat foods
Storing raw meat above cooked meat
Using the same cloth for all surfaces all day
Tasting food with the stirring spoon

questions.text: Give the stock-rotation rule that means older food is used before newer food (four letters, or the phrase).
questions.solution: FIFO (first in, first out) means older stock is used first, before it goes out of date
questions.hint: The food that arrives first is used first

questions.text: Which conditions do bacteria need in order to multiply?
questions.solution: Bacteria need warmth, moisture, food and time to multiply
questions.hint: Think about what the danger zone provides

questions.text: An uncooked dessert contains raw eggs. Which group is most at risk if the eggs carry Salmonella?
questions.solution: Vulnerable groups (pregnant women, babies and young children, older people and those who are ill) are most at risk
questions.hint: Think about people whose immune system is weaker

options: Pregnant women, babies, older people and people who are unwell
People who eat a lot of fruit

questions.text: Cooked food is going to be stored. Why should it be cooled quickly before it goes in the fridge?
questions.solution: Cooling quickly limits the time bacteria have to multiply in the danger zone
questions.hint: Think about what bacteria do between 5 °C and 63 °C

options: To reduce the time it spends in the danger zone
feedback: Cooling does not kill bacteria; it slows their growth

questions.text: Which statement about freezing food is accurate?
questions.solution: At −18 °C bacteria are dormant; they become active again as the food warms up
questions.hint: Are the bacteria killed or just 'asleep'?

options: Freezing makes bacteria dormant but does not kill them, so they can multiply again once the food thaws
Freezing removes all the moisture from food permanently
feedback: Freezing stops bacteria multiplying but does not kill them

questions.text: Which statement about reheating leftovers is accurate?
questions.solution: Reheat leftovers thoroughly to at least 75 °C in the centre, and only once
questions.hint: Think about the core temperature and how many times food is reheated

options: Leftovers can be reheated as many times as needed
Leftovers should be reheated until steaming hot in the centre (at least 75 °C) and reheated only once

questions.text: Why is Listeria a particular concern for pregnant women and older people?
questions.solution: Unlike most bacteria, Listeria multiplies at fridge temperatures; it can be very dangerous in pregnancy and for older people
questions.hint: Think about where Listeria can grow and who is most at risk

options: Listeria only grows in frozen food
Listeria can grow at fridge temperatures and can cause serious illness in vulnerable groups

questions.text: A takeaway keeps cooked rice at 30 °C for several hours. Which explanation is accurate?
questions.solution: 30 °C is inside the 5–63 °C danger zone; Bacillus cereus in cooked rice can produce toxins
questions.hint: Is 30 °C inside the danger zone?

options: 30 °C is cold enough to stop bacteria growing
Rice is a low-risk food, so this is safe
30 °C is in the danger zone, so bacteria such as Bacillus cereus can multiply and produce toxins

questions.text: Name the bacterium that comes mainly from human skin, noses and cuts and can produce toxins in food that has been handled a lot.
questions.solution: Staphylococcus aureus is found on skin and in noses; good personal hygiene reduces the risk
questions.hint: It is a round bacterium that grows in clusters like bunches of grapes

questions.text: Which statement about 'best before' dates is accurate?
questions.solution: Best before is about quality; food can still be safe to eat after it
questions.hint: Is this date mark about safety or quality?

options: Food may still be safe after the date if stored correctly, but its quality may be lower
Food must be thrown away the day after the date
Best before is the only date mark used on raw chicken
The date shows the day the food was made

questions.text: Raw chicken should not be washed because splashing water can spread which bacterium, found on much raw chicken?
questions.solution: Campylobacter is found on much raw chicken; washing it splashes the bacteria around the kitchen
questions.hint: It is the most common cause of bacterial food poisoning in the UK

feedback: Bacillus cereus is linked with cooked rice

questions.text: What are 'food miles'?
questions.solution: Food miles measure how far food travels from field or farm to plate
questions.hint: Think about a mango travelling to the UK

options: The distance food travels from where it is produced to where it is eaten
The energy content of a meal
How far a person walks to the shop
How long food can be stored

questions.text: What does 'seasonal food' mean?
questions.solution: Seasonal food is eaten at the time of year it naturally grows, such as UK strawberries in summer
questions.hint: Think about British strawberries in June

options: Food that is grown and harvested at its natural time of year
Food grown in heated greenhouses all year

questions.text: What is the term for knowing where food comes from and how it was grown, reared or caught? Give the term.
questions.solution: Provenance means where food comes from and how it was produced
questions.hint: It comes from a French word meaning 'to come from'

questions.text: How are ingredients listed on a UK food label?
questions.solution: Ingredients are listed in order of weight, with the largest amount first
questions.hint: Look at the first ingredient on a tin of tomato soup

options: In descending order of weight, largest first

questions.text: How many major allergens must be emphasised in the ingredients list on UK pre-packed food labels?
questions.solution: UK law lists 14 major allergens, such as peanuts, milk, eggs and gluten, which must be emphasised on labels
questions.hint: As well as nuts, milk and eggs, the list includes celery, mustard, sesame and lupin

questions.text: What does 'organic' mean on a food label?
questions.solution: Organic food is produced to strict standards that limit artificial chemicals and require high animal welfare
questions.hint: Think about how organic farmers control pests and feed the soil

options: Produced under strict rules that limit artificial pesticides and fertilisers

questions.text: Name the condition in which the body reacts to gluten, damaging the lining of the small intestine.
questions.solution: People with coeliac disease react to gluten and must avoid wheat, barley and rye
questions.hint: It begins with the letters 'coe'

questions.text: Which statement about a food allergy and a food intolerance is accurate?
questions.solution: A food allergy is an immune reaction that can cause anaphylaxis; an intolerance (such as lactose intolerance) is not an immune reaction
questions.hint: Which one can cause anaphylaxis?

options: An intolerance involves the immune system; an allergy does not
An allergy involves the immune system and can be life-threatening; an intolerance does not involve the immune system
Both are always mild and harmless
feedback: That is the wrong way round

questions.text: Which of these is an example of primary processing?
questions.solution: Primary processing turns raw food into something usable, such as milling wheat into flour
questions.hint: Primary processing is the first change to a raw food

options: Making pasta from flour and eggs
feedback: Making bread from flour is secondary processing

questions.text: People with lactose intolerance find it hard to digest the sugar in which food? Give the food.
questions.solution: Lactose is the sugar found in milk and dairy products
questions.hint: Lactose comes from the Latin word for this drink

questions.text: Which of these is an example of secondary processing?
questions.solution: Secondary processing turns primary-processed foods into other products, such as flour into bread
questions.hint: It uses a food that has already been processed once

feedback: Milling is primary processing
Pasteurising milk is primary processing

questions.text: Which dish is a traditional food of Japan?
questions.solution: Sushi (vinegared rice, often with raw fish) is a traditional Japanese food
questions.hint: This dish uses vinegared rice

feedback: Paella comes from Spain
Moussaka is Greek
Tagine comes from Morocco

questions.text: Give the term for a severe, life-threatening allergic reaction.
questions.solution: Anaphylaxis is a severe allergic reaction that needs emergency treatment, often with an adrenaline auto-injector
questions.hint: It begins with 'ana'

questions.text: Which type of vegetarian eats no animal products at all, including eggs, milk and honey?
questions.solution: Vegans eat no animal products; lacto-ovo vegetarians eat dairy and eggs; pescatarians eat fish
questions.hint: This diet avoids every animal product

feedback: Pescatarians eat fish

questions.text: A shopper in Kent wants apples with the lowest food miles. Which should they choose?
questions.solution: Local apples travel the shortest distance, so they have the lowest food miles
questions.hint: Which apples travel the shortest distance?

options: Apples from a farm in Kent

questions.text: A customer with a peanut allergy orders food in a café. What should the café do?
questions.solution: Allergy safety needs accurate information and preventing cross-contact, because tiny traces can cause a reaction
questions.hint: Even a tiny trace of peanut can cause a reaction

options: Pick visible peanuts off a dish just before serving
Tell the customer the food is probably fine
Give clear allergen information and prevent cross-contact with peanuts when preparing the food
feedback: Traces of peanut would remain and could cause a reaction

questions.text: A food label shows a red traffic light for salt. What does this mean?
questions.solution: Red means high, amber means medium and green means low
questions.hint: Think about traffic lights: what does red mean?

options: The food is high in salt
The food is medium in salt
feedback: Medium would be amber

questions.text: A family wants to reduce food waste. Which action would help?
questions.solution: Planning meals, using leftovers and storing food correctly all reduce waste
questions.hint: Think about buying only what you need

options: Buying extra food in case guests arrive
Planning meals and using up leftovers before buying more
Throwing away food on its best before date
Storing bread in a warm, damp place

questions.text: Many Muslims eat meat only if it has been prepared according to Islamic law. Give the term for food that is permitted.
questions.solution: Halal means permitted under Islamic law; many Muslims eat only halal meat and avoid pork
questions.hint: It is the opposite of haram

feedback.kosher: Kosher is the term used in Judaism

questions.text: Many Hindus avoid which meat in particular?
questions.solution: Many Hindus do not eat beef because the cow is regarded as sacred; many Hindus are vegetarian
questions.hint: Which animal is regarded as sacred by many Hindus?

questions.text: Which UK farm assurance logo, shaped like a farm vehicle, shows food was produced to British standards for safety, hygiene and animal welfare? Give the name.
questions.solution: The Red Tractor logo shows food meets UK farm assurance standards
questions.hint: It is named after a colour and a farm vehicle

questions.text: A ready meal label lists: water, tomatoes, pasta (6%), cheese, salt. Which statement is accurate?
questions.solution: Ingredients are listed in descending order of weight, so water (listed first) is the largest ingredient
questions.hint: Remember the rule for the order of ingredients

options: There is more pasta than tomatoes
Cheese makes up more than half the meal
There is more water than any other ingredient
feedback: Tomatoes are listed before pasta, so there are more tomatoes

questions.text: Why might a chef choose UK strawberries in summer rather than imported ones in winter?
questions.solution: Seasonal local produce is fresher, usually cheaper and travels a shorter distance
questions.hint: Think about freshness, cost and distance travelled

options: In season they are fresher, often cheaper, full of flavour and have lower food miles
UK strawberries are only legal to sell in summer
Strawberries cannot be eaten in winter

questions.text: A food carries the Fairtrade mark. What does this tell the shopper?
questions.solution: Fairtrade aims to give farmers in developing countries a fair price and better working conditions
questions.hint: Think about the people who grew the food

options: The food was produced in the UK
The farmers who grew it were paid a fair price and work in better conditions
feedback: Fairtrade is about fair pay and conditions; organic is a separate label

questions.text: Which UK law, named after a teenager, requires food made and pre-packed on the premises to show a full ingredients list with allergens emphasised? Give the name.
questions.solution: Natasha's Law (from October 2021) covers food pre-packed for direct sale
questions.hint: It is known by a girl's first name followed by the word 'Law'

questions.text: A food label says 'May contain nuts'. What does this mean?
questions.solution: 'May contain' warns of possible cross-contact, so people with a nut allergy should avoid the food
questions.hint: The warning is about traces from the factory, not the recipe

options: The food has been tested and contains no nuts
Nuts are not an ingredient, but the food may have been in contact with nuts during production

questions.text: Which choice would reduce the carbon footprint of a meal?
questions.solution: Local, seasonal food usually needs less transport and less energy for heated greenhouses
questions.hint: Think about transport and energy use

options: Buying food flown in by air
Leaving the oven on after cooking

questions.text: Give the name of the clay oven used in Indian cooking to make naan bread and tikka.
questions.solution: A tandoor is a very hot clay oven used for naan and tandoori dishes
questions.hint: Tandoori chicken is named after it

questions.text: Which statement about buying local food is accurate?
questions.solution: Local food usually reduces food miles and supports the local economy, but 'always' statements are not accurate
questions.hint: Be careful with statements that say 'always'

options: Local food usually has fewer food miles and supports local farmers, although it may cost more
Local food always has a lower carbon footprint than any imported food
Local food always contains more vitamins

questions.text: A person with coeliac disease is eating out. Which choice is suitable?
questions.solution: Wheat pasta, bread and batter contain gluten; plain fish, potatoes and vegetables do not
questions.hint: Which ingredients in each meal contain gluten?

options: Grilled fish with potatoes and vegetables, with no flour-based sauce
A sandwich made with wheat bread
feedback: Batter is usually made with wheat flour, which contains gluten

questions.text: Why is milk pasteurised?
questions.solution: Pasteurisation heats milk to about 72 °C for 15 seconds and then cools it quickly, killing harmful bacteria
questions.hint: It is named after Louis Pasteur, who studied bacteria

options: Pasteurised milk lasts for years without a fridge
Heating to about 72 °C for 15 seconds kills harmful bacteria and extends shelf life with little change in taste
feedback: Pasteurised milk must still be kept in the fridge

questions.text: Why might a vegetarian who eats eggs and dairy still need to plan their iron intake?
questions.solution: Non-haem iron from plants is less easily absorbed, so eating it with vitamin C helps
questions.hint: Compare iron from plants with iron from red meat

options: Plant foods contain no iron at all
Iron from plant foods (non-haem iron) is less easily absorbed than iron from meat

questions.text: Give the name of the Middle Eastern dip made from chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice and garlic.
questions.solution: Hummus is made from chickpeas blended with tahini (sesame paste), lemon juice and garlic
questions.hint: It is often eaten with pitta bread

questions.text: Which statement about seasonal food is accurate?
questions.solution: Food eaten in season is usually fresher and cheaper and needs less storage or transport
questions.hint: Watch out for 'all' and 'always'

options: Seasonal food is often fresher, as it has not been stored or transported for long
Seasonal food can only be bought at farmers' markets
All food in UK supermarkets is seasonal
Seasonal food is always more expensive

questions.text: Many Jewish people keep kosher. Which practice is part of keeping kosher?
questions.solution: Kosher food laws include not mixing meat with dairy and not eating pork or shellfish
questions.hint: Think about which food groups are kept apart

options: Not eating meat and dairy foods together
Avoiding beef because the cow is sacred
feedback: Some Christians avoid meat on Fridays; this is not a kosher rule
Many Hindus avoid beef; kosher laws allow beef from animals slaughtered in the kosher way
